mainTopic: Paying workers on time: middlemen, day and night workers, עושק versus גזל, and the משנה on ביומו תתן שכרו and בל תלין
overview: This amud starts by finishing a ברייתא about a middleman who hires workers for someone else. If he tells them 'your pay is on the owner,' neither he nor the owner violates בל תלין, and אמוראים actually hired workers this way. רבה בר רב הונא adds that the market merchants of סורא do not violate בל תלין, because everyone knows they pay on market day, but they do violate בל תשהא if they wait longer. Next, רב and שמואל argue about when a night hourly worker must be paid, and רב's view is defended as matching רבי יהודה in a ברייתא. That ברייתא lists five לאוין and one עשה for withholding wages, and רב חסדא explains that the list covers the whole topic, not one single act. The גמרא then asks how עושק differs from גזל: רב חסדא, רב ששת and אביי each define them, and רבא says they are really the same act listed twice to add a second לאו. A new משנה follows: wages for people, animals and utensils all fall under both prohibitions, but only when the worker demanded payment. A worker who claims on time swears and collects, and a גר תושב gets only ביומו תתן שכרו. The גמרא begins asking whose view this משנה follows and starts quoting a ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the middleman is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by explaining that the middleman does not violate בל תלין because the work was not done for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this one (the middleman) is exempt, because the work was not done for him.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the ברייתא about a person who sends a friend to hire workers for him. This line explains why the friend, the middleman, does not violate בל תלין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says neither person violates בל תלין, and each has his own reason. The middleman's reason is that the workers were not working for him. The next step will question this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah ban on holding back a worker's pay overnight
His work, meaning the work the worker did

phrases.english: And this one, because his work is not for him.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the middleman who hired the workers for his friend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The middleman does not violate בל תלין, since the work was not done for him.

steps.title: If the middleman promised to pay, he should be responsible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case this is. If the middleman said 'your pay is on me,' a ברייתא shows he is fully responsible, so he should violate בל תלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he told them 'your pay is on me,' then the pay really is on him. As a ברייתא teaches: if someone hires a worker to work in his own field and then shows him a friend's field, he must pay the worker in full. Afterward he collects from the field owner the value of the benefit the owner received.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reason for exempting the middleman. It uses a second ברייתא to show that a hirer who takes the payment on himself stays fully responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second ברייתא the worker's labor helped someone else, yet the hirer still pays the full wage. So the fact that the work was 'not for him' does not free a person who promised to pay. If so, why should the middleman in our ברייתא be exempt from בל תלין?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
The value of the benefit he gave him

steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא, 'בעל הבית' does not mean the hirer. It means the owner of the friend's field, where the work was actually done.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he said to them: your pay is on me,
then the pay is his responsibility,
as it is taught: one who hires a worker
to work in his own field
and showed him his friend's field instead,
gives him his full pay,
and then goes back and takes from the field owner
the value of the benefit he gave him!
phrases.notes: The field owner pays only for the benefit he got, not the full wage. The hirer is the one fully on the hook.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ שְׂכַרְכֶם עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason given in Step 1 for exempting the middleman.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exemption of the middleman from בל תלין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that a hirer who said 'your pay is on me' must pay in full even when the work helped someone else. So the middleman should be responsible and should violate בל תלין.

steps.title: He said the pay is on the owner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a middleman who told the workers that the owner will pay them.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is where he told them: your pay is on the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by defining the exact case of our ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middleman never took the payment on himself, so he is not responsible and does not violate בל תלין. The owner is also exempt, because he did not hire the workers himself. That fits the ברייתא's statement that neither one violates the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

steps.whatToRemember: A middleman who says 'your pay is on the owner' avoids בל תלין for both people. One who says 'your pay is on me' is fully responsible.

phrases.english: It is needed only where he said to them:
Your pay is on the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The middleman said 'your pay is on me,' which would make him responsible.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said 'your pay is on the owner,' so he took on no obligation.

steps.title: אמוראים who used this method in practice
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בר מרימר had his attendant hire workers in this way, and מרימר and מר זוטרא hired workers for each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בר מרימר told his attendant: Go hire workers for me and tell them, 'Your pay is on the owner.' מרימר and מר זוטרא used to hire workers for each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that אמוראים actually used the method from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiring through someone else, with the words 'your pay is on the owner,' means nobody is in danger of בל תלין if the pay comes late. מרימר and מר זוטרא did the same thing by each hiring workers for the other.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule is a real, practical way to avoid בל תלין.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בַּר מָרִימָר אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Yehuda bar Mareimar said to his attendant:
Go hire workers for me,
and say to them:
Your pay is on the owner.
Mareimar and Mar Zutra would hire for each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה בַּר מָרִימָר אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the conclusion of Step 3 being used in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, hiring through someone who says 'your pay is on the owner' avoids בל תלין.

steps.title: The market merchants of סורא who pay on market day
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says the merchants of the סורא market do not violate בל תלין, since everyone knows they pay on market day. If they delay past that, they do violate בל תשהא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: The market people of סורא do not violate בל תלין, because everyone knows they depend on market day to pay. But they certainly violate בל תשהא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement about workers who know from the start that they will be paid later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תלין applies only when the worker expects his pay right away. Here everyone knows the pay comes on market day, so there is no expectation of being paid the same day. If the employer holds back the pay even after market day, he violates the separate איסור of בל תשהא.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not delay, a separate איסור against holding back payment

steps.whatToRemember: When the workers know payment will come later, there is no בל תלין. Holding back beyond the expected time is still בל תשהא.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
These market people of Sura
do not violate 'do not delay overnight,'
since they surely know
that they rely on market day,
phrases.notes: The workers know the employer gets his money on market day, so they don't expect pay until then.

phrases.english: but because of 'do not hold back,'
he certainly violates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: הָנֵי שׁוּקָאֵי דְּסוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case that still deals with בל תלין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When pay is known to come on market day, there is no בל תלין, but delaying beyond that is בל תשהא.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about the night hourly worker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a שכיר שעות collects all night and all day. רב says a day worker collects during the day and a night worker during the night. שמואל agrees about the day worker, but says a night worker collects during the night and the whole next day too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: an hourly worker collects all night and all day. רב says: an hourly worker by day collects all that day; an hourly worker by night collects all that night. שמואל says: an hourly worker by day collects all that day; an hourly worker by night collects all that night and all the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about hourly workers and brings a disagreement between רב and שמואל about what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Collects all night' means the employer has that whole period to pay before he violates בל תלין. רב and שמואל agree about the day worker. They argue only about the night worker. Does he get paid only during that night (רב), or also through the next day (שמואל)?

keyTerms.meaning: A worker hired for a few hours, not a full day or night
Collects his pay. The time when he collects is the employer's window to pay without sinning
Of the day / of the night, meaning when he did his work

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the night worker is paid that night only. שמואל says that night plus the next day.

phrases.english: An hourly worker collects
all night and all day.
Rav said: an hourly worker of the day
collects all the day,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת דְּלַיְלָה – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: an hourly worker of the night collects all the night.
And Shmuel said: an hourly worker of the day
collects all the day,
and an hourly worker of the night
collects all the night and all the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after the discussion of the סורא market merchants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a night hourly worker is paid that night only. שמואל: that night and the next day.

steps.title: The משנה seems to refute רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says an hourly worker collects 'all night and all day.' That sounds like שמואל, so it seems to be a refutation of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: an hourly worker collects all night and all day. This is a refutation of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב using the plain words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts 'all night' and 'all day' together for the same worker. It sounds like the night worker has the night and the next day too, which is exactly שמואל's view. רב said the night worker only has the night.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation from a source

phrases.english: We learned: an hourly worker collects
all night and all day,
a refutation of Rav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's position from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a night hourly worker collects only during the night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives 'night and day' together, which sounds like the night worker gets the following day as well.

steps.title: רב reads the משנה as two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the משנה is speaking about two different cases. 'All night' is for the night worker, and 'all day' is for the day worker.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can say to you: the משנה teaches two separate cases. An hourly worker by day collects all day, and an hourly worker by night collects all night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by rereading the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All night and all day' is not one window of time for one worker. It is a short way of listing two cases. Each worker gets the time period that matches when he worked.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches 'to the sides': two separate cases are packed into one sentence
He could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Night and day' here does NOT mean one worker gets both. Each part of the phrase belongs to a different worker.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
it is teaching separate sides (cases).

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת דְּיוֹם – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: an hourly worker of the day collects all the day,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת דְּלַיְלָה – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: an hourly worker of the night collects all the night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives one worker both the night and the day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists two workers: night for the night worker and day for the day worker.

steps.title: A second משנה clearly gives the night worker the next day too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another line of the משנה. For workers hired by the week, month, year, or seven-year cycle, one who finishes at night collects all night and all day. That cannot be split into separate cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if he was hired by the week, month, year, or seven-year cycle and he left during the day, he collects all day. If he left at night, he collects all night and all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב again, this time from a line that does not allow the 'two separate cases' answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה itself already separates the day case from the night case. It still gives the night case 'all night and all day.' So the night worker clearly has until the end of the next day, which goes against רב's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: A worker hired for a week
A worker hired for a seven-year cycle
Leaves, meaning he finishes his term of work

phrases.english: We learned: if he was a worker hired for a week,
phrases.notes: Watch out: here שבת means a week, and שבוע below means a seven-year cycle.

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר חֹדֶשׁ, שְׂכִיר שָׁנָה, שְׂכִיר שָׁבוּעַ,
phrases.english: a worker for a month, a worker for a year, a worker for a seven-year cycle,
if he leaves in the day, he collects all the day.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצֵא בַּלַּיְלָה – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה וְכׇל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: If he leaves at night, he collects all the night and all the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב that gets around the answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a night worker has only the night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This line already separates day from night and still gives the night case 'night and day.' So the 'separate cases' reading cannot work here.

steps.title: רב: this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that תנאים disagree about this. A ברייתא records that רבי יהודה holds like רב: the night worker collects only at night. רבי שמעון holds like שמואל. רב follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can say to you: it is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches. An hourly worker by day collects all day, and an hourly worker by night collects all night; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: an hourly worker by day collects all day, and an hourly worker by night collects all night and all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by showing that his view has support from a תנא, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not have to fit every משנה, because the issue is an open argument among the תנאים. The משנה that challenged him matches רבי שמעון's view. רב simply follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute of תנאים
These are the words of רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: רב follows רבי יהודה (night worker: night only). שמואל matches רבי שמעון (night worker: night plus the next day).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא defends an אמורא: when a source goes against him, it shows that his view is one side of an argument among the תנאים.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you: it is a dispute of Tannaim,
as it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת דְּיוֹם – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: an hourly worker of the day collects all the day,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת דְּלַיְלָה – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה,
phrases.english: an hourly worker of the night collects all the night,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת דְּיוֹם – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: an hourly worker of the day collects all the day,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת דְּלַיְלָה – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה וְכׇל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: an hourly worker of the night collects all the night and all the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is the only voice, so רב is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds like רב. The משנה follows רבי שמעון, so רב is not refuted.

steps.title: Withholding wages breaks five prohibitions and one positive command
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that one who withholds a worker's pay violates five לאוין and one עשה, and lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here the Sages said: anyone who holds back a hired worker's pay violates these five prohibitions and one positive command: 'Do not oppress your neighbor,' 'Do not steal,' 'Do not oppress a poor hired worker,' 'Do not keep wages overnight,' 'Give him his pay on his day,' and 'The sun shall not set on him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its discussion of paying workers on time with a summary. Holding back wages breaks a whole list of מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six items are listed. Five are לאוין, and one is the עשה of ביומו תתן שכרו. This shows how seriously the Torah treats delaying a worker's pay.

keyTerms.meaning: One who holds back or withholds (money owed)

phrases.english: From here they said:
Anyone who withholds a hired worker's wages
violates these five prohibitions and a positive command.
phrases.notes: The list below has six items: five 'don'ts' plus the one 'do,' which is 'give him his pay on his day.'

phrases.english: because of 'Do not oppress your neighbor,'
and because of 'Do not steal,'
and because of 'Do not oppress a poor hired worker,'
and because of 'Do not keep it overnight,'
and because of 'On his day you shall give his wages,'
and because of 'The sun shall not set on him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: כׇּל הַכּוֹבֵשׁ שְׂכַר שָׂכִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא about day and night workers with its summary of all the prohibitions involved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Withholding a hired worker's wages violates five לאוין and one עשה.

steps.title: Day prohibitions and night prohibitions cannot all apply together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the list: some prohibitions apply only by day and others only by night, so one person cannot violate them all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ones that apply by day do not apply by night, and the ones that apply by night do not apply by day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's statement that one person breaks all of these prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the earlier steps we know a day worker must be paid by night and a night worker by day. בל תלין fits one case and לא תבא עליו השמש fits the other. So no single act of withholding can violate the whole list.

phrases.english: Those that apply by day do not apply by night,
and those that apply by night do not apply by day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 11 that one person violates all the listed prohibitions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that one who withholds wages violates all five לאוין and the עשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The day prohibitions and the night prohibitions belong to different cases, so they can never all apply at the same time.

steps.title: The list describes the general topic of wages
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the ברייתא is listing every prohibition connected to the topic of wages, not claiming one person breaks them all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is just the general category of hiring.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not describing one single act of withholding. It is listing all the prohibitions that belong to the general topic of a worker's wages. Each case triggers only the ones that fit its timing.

keyTerms.meaning: The general category or topic of hired work

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is merely the general category of hiring.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שֵׁם שְׂכִירוּת בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the scope of the ברייתא's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a single person violates every prohibition at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lists all the prohibitions in the general topic of wages. Each case triggers only some of them.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'five prohibitions and one עשה' describe the whole subject of withholding wages, not one single act.

steps.title: What is the difference between עושק and גזל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how עושק differs from גזל, since both appear in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'oppression' and what is 'stealing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both בל תעשק and בל תגזל appear in the list from step 11, so they must be two different wrongs. The גמרא wants to know what separates them.

keyTerms.meaning: Oppression; wrongfully holding back money owed

phrases.english: What is oppression
and what is stealing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about two terms from the list in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of עושק and גזל, and what separates them.

steps.title: רב חסדא: putting him off versus openly refusing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says עושק is repeatedly telling the worker to come back later, and גזל is admitting the debt but refusing to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: 'Go and come back, go and come back' is oppression. 'I have your money, but I won't give it to you' is stealing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by giving a case for each term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the employer admits he owes the money. עושק is stalling: he keeps sending the worker away with promises. גזל is an open refusal to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Go and come back (putting someone off)
I have what belongs to you

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
'Go and come back, go and come back' is oppression.
'You have money in my hands

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ״ – זֶה הוּא גָּזֵל.
phrases.english: and I am not giving it to you' is stealing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֵךְ וָשׁוּב לֵךְ וָשׁוּב זֶה הוּא עוֹשֶׁק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עושק is stalling the worker with 'come back later.' גזל is admitting the debt while refusing to pay.

steps.title: רב ששת: the תורה's עושק must involve denying the debt
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects that the עושק which requires a קרבן is like denying a פקדון, where the person denies owing the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת challenged this: What is the oppression for which the תורה requires a קרבן? It is like a deposit, where he denies owing the money!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב חסדא's definition of עושק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires a קרבן for עושק, and it lists עושק together with denying a פקדון. That means עושק involves denying the debt. In רב חסדא's 'go and come back' case, the employer admits he owes the money, so it cannot be the תורה's עושק.

keyTerms.meaning: An item or money left in someone's care

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet challenged it:
What is the oppression
for which the Torah requires an offering?
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 5:21–25, where עושק is listed next to denying a פקדון.

phrases.english: It is similar to a deposit,
where he denies owing him the money!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אֵיזֶהוּ עוֹשֶׁק שֶׁחִיְּיבָה עָלָיו תּוֹרָה קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's definition of עושק from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's definition of עושק as 'go and come back.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah's עושק carries a קרבן and is grouped with denying a פקדון, so it must involve denial. 'Go and come back' is an admission of the debt.

steps.title: רב ששת: 'I already paid you' is עושק
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives a new definition: עושק is falsely claiming 'I already paid you,' while גזל stays as openly refusing to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said: 'I already gave it to you' is oppression. 'I have your money, but I won't give it to you' is stealing.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of his challenge, רב ששת replaces רב חסדא's definition of עושק with his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I already paid you' is a denial of the debt. That matches the Torah's עושק, which is like denying a פקדון. רב ששת keeps גזל the same as רב חסדא: openly admitting the debt and refusing to pay.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת, עושק is denying the debt ('I already paid'), and גזל is admitting it but refusing to pay.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת does not argue about גזל. He only changes the definition of עושק.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said:
'I gave it to you' is oppression,

phrases.aramaic: ״יֵשׁ לְךָ בְּיָדִי וְאֵינִי נוֹתֵן לָךְ״ – זֶה הוּא גָּזֵל.
phrases.english: 'You have money in my hands and I am not giving it to you' is stealing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: נְתַתִּיו לָךְ זֶהוּ עוֹשֶׁק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a replacement answer to step 14, based on the challenge of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עושק is denying the debt by claiming 'I already paid you.' גזל is admitting the debt but refusing to pay.

steps.title: אביי objects that stealing also needs a denial
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the גזל which requires a קרבן must also be like a denied פקדון. So openly refusing to pay cannot be the definition of גזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenges this: The גזל for which the תורה requires a קרבן must be like a פקדון, where the person denies owing the money!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the same argument רב ששת used against עושק and applies it to גזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said the עושק that brings a קרבן must involve denying the money, like a פקדון. אביי says the same is true of גזל, because it appears in the same פסוק about קרבנות. So 'I won't pay you,' which admits the debt, cannot be the definition of גזל either.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it (raises a strong objection)
Similar to, in the same pattern as

phrases.english: Abaye objects to this:
What is the stealing
for which the Torah obligated an offering?
phrases.notes: This is the גזל in ויקרא 5:21, where a false oath about money requires a קרבן.

phrases.english: We need it to be similar to a deposit,
where he denies the money to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב ששת's own objection (step 16) to the definition of גזל that he kept from רב חסדא (step 17).
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of גזל as admitting the debt but refusing to pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גזל sits in the same קרבן פסוק as פקדון, so it must also involve a denial. Openly refusing to pay is not a denial.

steps.title: אביי's definitions: 'I never hired you' versus 'I paid you'
steps.stepSummary: אביי defines both terms as kinds of denial. עושק is denying ever hiring the worker. גזל is claiming the wages were already paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: 'I never hired you' is עושק. 'I already gave it to you' is גזל.
steps.whatsHappening: Since both terms must involve a denial, אביי gives two new definitions that are both denials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both עושק and גזל fit the פקדון pattern of denying money. The difference is what is denied. In עושק he denies the whole job, and in גזל he admits the job but says he already paid.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch: רב ששת called 'I paid you' עושק, but אביי calls the same claim גזל.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
'I never hired you' is oppression;
'I gave it to you' is stealing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives new definitions after the objection in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עושק is 'I never hired you,' and גזל is 'I already paid you.' Both are denials, like a פקדון.

steps.title: Why did רב ששת object only to oppression?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב ששת applied the denial argument to עושק but not to גזל, since אביי's objection was the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב ששת, why was עושק a difficulty for him, while גזל was not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רב ששת was consistent. He kept רב חסדא's definition of גזל, even though it has no denial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת insisted that עושק must be a denial. Yet he left גזל as 'refusing to pay,' which is exactly what אביי attacked. So the גמרא asks what made גזל different in his eyes.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Sheshet, what is different about oppression
that it was difficult for him,
and what is different about stealing
that it was not difficult for him?
phrases.notes: Why didn't רב ששת raise the same objection against גזל that אביי just raised?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב ששת's view in light of אביי's objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת keeping רב חסדא's definition of גזל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The denial argument should apply equally to גזל, so treating the two differently looks inconsistent.

steps.title: רב ששת's stealing: refusing first, then denying
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת would explain that his גזל case also ends in a denial. First the employer refuses to pay, and later he denies the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: גזל is where he first stole from him by refusing to pay, and afterward denied owing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. His גזל case also includes a denial, so it fits the פקדון pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I won't pay you' is only the first stage. The קרבן comes when he later denies owing the money. So רב ששת's גזל fits the פקדון pattern after all.

keyTerms.meaning: He would tell you (how the person would answer)
And afterward denied it to him

phrases.english: He would say to you:
Stealing is where he stole from him and then denied it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so that it includes a later denial
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's גזל is just refusing to pay, with no denial.
steps.terutzMaskana: His גזל is refusing first and denying later, so it does involve a denial.

steps.title: Then oppression could also be admitting and later denying
steps.stepSummary: If גזל can be 'admit, then deny,' עושק could be read the same way. Then רב ששת would not need the 'I paid you' definition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, עושק could also be where he later denied it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The same 'later denial' fix could have saved רב חסדא's definition of עושק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said עושק is 'come back later.' If a later denial can be added to גזל, it could be added to עושק too. Then רב ששת's objection to רב חסדא's עושק would fall away.

phrases.english: If so,
even oppression too could be where he later denied it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 21 by applying it to עושק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the explanation works for גזל, it should work for עושק too. Then רב ששת had no reason to reject רב חסדא's עושק.

steps.title: The verse's wording separates the two cases
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'או בגזל,' a denial about something stolen earlier. But it says 'או עשק,' which means the oppression itself is the sin, so it cannot be a later denial.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? For גזל the פסוק writes 'או בגזל,' which shows he first admitted the debt. But for עושק, does it write 'או בעושק'? It writes 'או עשק,' meaning he already oppressed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the exact wording of the פסוק in ויקרא, showing why only גזל can be 'admit first, deny later.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In a matter of גזל' describes the denial as being about money that was gotten earlier through גזל. That allows a two-stage case: first the stealing, then the denial. 'או עשק' is a verb for the sin itself, so the act of oppression is the denial. That is why רב ששת needs 'I already paid you' for עושק.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a small difference in a פסוק's grammar ('בגזל' versus 'עשק') can define a whole legal case.

phrases.english: How can you compare?
Granted, there it is written: 'or in a matter of robbery,'
which shows that he admitted to him at first.
But regarding oppression,
is it written 'or in a matter of oppression'?
'Or he oppressed' is written, meaning that he already oppressed him.
phrases.notes: The oppression is the denial itself, not an earlier stage that comes before a denial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the exact wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עושק and גזל can both be explained as admitting first and denying later.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'בגזל' allows an earlier admission. 'עשק' as a verb means the oppression itself is the denial.

steps.title: רבא: oppression and stealing are the same act
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there is no real difference between עושק and גזל. The תורה lists them separately so the person breaks two לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: עושק is the same as גזל. Why did the פסוק divide them? So that he breaks two prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes a completely different approach. He drops the search for a difference between the two terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the earlier opinions tried to find two separate cases. רבא says they are one act with two names. The extra name adds a second לאו for the same wrongdoing.
steps.whatToRemember: Four views on the two terms. רב חסדא: עושק is 'come back later,' and גזל is refusing to pay. רב ששת: עושק is 'I paid you,' and גזל is refusing first, then denying. אביי: עושק is 'I never hired you,' and גזל is 'I paid you.' רבא: they are the same, and the two names make two לאוין.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is oppression, this is stealing.
And why did the verse divide them?
So that he violates two prohibitions for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a completely different answer to the original question in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עושק and גזל are the same act. They are written separately so that the one who withholds wages breaks two לאוין.

steps.title: Wages for people, animals, and utensils all fall under both prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that wages for a person, an animal, or utensils are all covered by 'ביומו תתן שכרו' and by 'לא תלין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether it is a person's wages, rent for an animal, or rent for utensils, it falls under 'On his day you shall give his wages' and under 'The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you overnight until morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that paying on time applies not only to a worker's wages but also to rent for an animal or for utensils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two פסוקים about paying on time: 'ביומו תתן שכרו' in דברים and 'לא תלין' in ויקרא. The משנה says both apply to all three kinds of hiring. One could have thought they apply only to a human worker.

keyTerms.meaning: Wages, or the rent paid for something
'On his day you shall give his wages' (דברים 24:15)

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא is about to ask whose view this is. That question depends on these two rulings: animals and utensils get both לאוין, and a גר תושב (step 28) gets only one.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Whether the wages of a person
or the rent for an animal
or the rent for utensils –
it falls under 'On his day you shall give his wages,'
and it falls under

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תָלִין פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר אִתְּךָ עַד בֹּקֶר״.
phrases.english: 'The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you overnight until morning.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד שְׂכַר אָדָם וְאֶחָד שְׂכַר בְּהֵמָה וְאֶחָד שְׂכַר כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the עושק/גזל discussion ended with רבא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wages for a person, an animal, or utensils are covered by both ביומו תתן שכרו and לא תלין.

steps.title: He only transgresses if the worker asked to be paid
steps.stepSummary: The לאוין apply only when the worker demanded payment. Sending him to a storekeeper or money changer to collect also avoids the transgression.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does he transgress? When the worker demanded payment from him. If he did not demand it, the employer does not transgress. If the employer sent him to a storekeeper or a money changer to be paid, he does not transgress.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets limits on the prohibitions. They apply only if the worker asked for his pay, and not if the employer arranged for someone else to pay him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Delaying payment is only a sin when the worker wants the money and is being held back. If he never asked, or if the employer sent him to a shopkeeper or money changer to collect, the employer is not holding his wages back.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent him over (to collect from someone else)

phrases.english: When? When he demanded it from him.
If he did not demand it, he does not transgress it.
If he sent him over to a storekeeper
phrases.notes: The employer told the worker to go collect his pay from the storekeeper.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵצֶל שׁוּלְחָנִי – אֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו.
phrases.english: or to a money changer, he does not transgress it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits when the two לאוין from step 25 actually apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He transgresses only if the worker demanded payment. Not demanding, or being sent to a storekeeper or money changer, means no transgression.

steps.title: A worker who claims on time swears and collects
steps.stepSummary: A hired worker who claims his pay within its time may swear and collect. After that time he may not, unless witnesses saw him claim on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hired worker within his time swears and takes. If his time has passed, he does not swear and take. If there are witnesses that he demanded it within his time, he swears and takes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a related rule. A worker who asks for his pay on time can collect by swearing, even if the employer says he already paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the one making a claim must prove it, but here the worker swears and collects. This works only within the payment time. After it passes he loses this, unless witnesses saw him demand payment on time.

keyTerms.meaning: Within his time (the time the pay is due)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the worker, not the employer, is the one who swears, and then he collects. Usually it works the other way around.

phrases.english: A hired worker within his time swears and takes.
phrases.notes: This is where the employer says, 'I already paid you.'

phrases.english: If his time has passed, he does not swear and take.
If there are witnesses that he demanded it from him within his time,
then he swears and takes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related rule about how a worker collects disputed wages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Within his time, a worker swears and collects. After it, he does not, unless witnesses saw him demand payment on time.

steps.title: A גר תושב gets only one of the two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: Paying a גר תושב falls under 'ביומו תתן שכרו' but not under 'לא תלין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גר תושב falls under 'On his day you shall give his wages,' but does not fall under 'The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you overnight until morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by splitting the two prohibitions. For a גר תושב worker only one of them applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the two לאוין went together. Here the משנה says only 'ביומו תתן שכרו' applies to a גר תושב. This split is one of the points the גמרא will use to figure out whose view the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who keeps the seven מצוות of the children of נח

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rulings: both לאוין apply to wages for people, animals, and utensils. They apply only if the worker demanded payment. A worker who demands on time swears and collects. A גר תושב gets only 'ביומו תתן שכרו'.

phrases.english: A גר תושב
falls under 'On his day you shall give his wages,'
but does not fall under

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תָלִין פְּעוּלַּת שָׂכִיר אִתְּךָ עַד בֹּקֶר״.
phrases.english: 'The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you overnight until morning.'

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם בְּיוֹמוֹ תִּתֵּן שְׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a case where only one of the two לאוין from step 25 applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר תושב is covered by ביומו תתן שכרו but not by לא תלין.

steps.title: Whose opinion does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows. It notes that the משנה matches neither the תנא קמא of 'מאחיך' nor רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Whose is our משנה? It is not the first תנא of 'from your brothers,' and it is not רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking which תנא wrote the משנה. It points out that the משנה does not fit either of the two opinions it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made specific choices about which cases get which לאוין. The גמרא says those choices fit neither the תנא קמא nor רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It has not yet shown why; the ברייתא it quotes next will lay out their two views.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Whose is our משנה?
It is not the first תנא of 'from your brothers,'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:14. This is the first opinion in a ברייתא about that פסוק, quoted right after this.

phrases.english: and it is not רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking whose view it follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the משנה's rulings follow, since they seem to fit neither the תנא קמא of מאחיך nor רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: Setting up the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברייתא it means and starts to quote it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it? As it was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote the ברייתא where the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 mentioned two opinions without explaining them. Here the גמרא introduces the source with 'דתניא' so we can see their views and check them against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (which source is meant)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He means: which ברייתא are we talking about?

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the ברייתא behind the two opinions named in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברייתא with the views of the תנא קמא of מאחיך and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
